question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X\sim N(1.8, \sigma^2)$ and $P(X \geq 4) = 0.2119,$ find $\sigma^2,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

$z$$\, 0.00 \,$$\, 0.01 \,$$\, 0.02 \,$
$\, 0.7 \,$ $\, 0.7580 \,$ $\, 0.7611 \,$ $\, 0.7642 \,$
$\, 0.8 \,$ $\, 0.7881 \,$ $\, 0.7910 \,$ $\, 0.7939 \,$
$\, 0.9 \,$ $\, 0.8159 \,$ $\, 0.8186 \,$ $\, 0.8212 \,$
question.explanation:
First, we convert the given probability into a cumulative probability using the complement:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq 4) &= 1 - P(X \geq 4) \\[3pt] &= 1 - 0.2119 \\[3pt] &= 0.7881 \end{align*} \]

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq 4) &= 0.7881 \\[5pt] P \left( Z \leq \dfrac{4 - 1.8}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.7881 \\[5pt] \Phi \left( \dfrac{2.2}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.7881 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2.2}{\sigma} &= \Phi^{-1} (0.7881) \\[5pt] \end{align*} \]

According to the table, we have

\[ \Phi(0.80) = 0.7881 \quad \Rightarrow \quad \Phi^{-1}( 0.7881) = 0.80. \]

Therefore, we have

\[ \begin{align*} \dfrac{2.2}{\sigma} &= 0.80 \\[5pt] \sigma &= \dfrac{2.2}{0.80} \\[5pt] \sigma &= 2.75. \\[5pt] \end{align*} \]

Finally, \[ \begin{align} \sigma^2 = 2.75^2 = 7. 56 \end{align} \] to $2$ decimal places.

question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X\sim N(-1, \sigma^2)$ and $P(X \lt -3.1) = 0.3632,$ find $\sigma.$

$z$ $\, 0.03 \,$ $\, 0.04 \,$ $\, 0.05 \,$
$\, -0.5\,$ $\,0.2981 \,$ $\,0.2946 \,$ $\,0.2912 \,$
$\, -0.4 \,$ $\,0.3336 \,$ $\,0.3300 \,$ $\,0.3264 \,$
$\, -0.3 \,$ $\, 0.3707 \,$ $\, 0.3669 \,$ $\, 0.3632 \,$
question.explanation:
First, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

\begin{align*} P(X \lt -3.1) &= 0.3632 \\[5pt] P \left( Z \lt \dfrac{-3.1-(-1)}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.3632 \\[5pt] \Phi \left(- \dfrac{2.1}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.3632 \\[5pt] -\dfrac{2.1}{\sigma} &= \Phi^{-1} (0.3632) \\[5pt] \end{align*}

According to the table, we have

\[ \Phi(-0.35) = 0.3632 \quad \Rightarrow \quad \Phi^{-1}(0.3632) = -0.35. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} -\dfrac{2.1}{\sigma} &= -0.35 \\[5pt] %\sigma &= \dfrac{-2.1}{-0.35} \\[5pt] \sigma &= 6. \\[5pt] \end{align*}

question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ is a normal random variable with $P(|X| \lt 2) = 0.6826,$ find $\sigma^2.$

$z$ $\, 0.00 \,$ $\, 0.01 \,$ $\, 0.02 \,$
$\, 1.0 \,$ $\, 0.8413 \,$ $\, 0.8438 \,$ $\, 0.8461 \,$
$\, 1.1 \,$ $\, 0.8643 \,$ $\, 0.8665 \,$ $\, 0.8686 \,$
$\, 1.2 \,$ $\, 0.8849 \,$ $\, 0.8869 \,$ $\, 0.8888 \,$
question.explanation:
First, we express the given probability as \[ P ( |X| \lt 2) = P(-2 < X < 2) . \]

Then, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

\[\begin{align*} P(-2 < X < 2) &= 0.6826 \\[5pt] 2 P(0 < X < 2) &= 0.6826 \\[5pt] P(0 < X < 2) &= 0.3413\\[5pt] P(X < 2) - P(X < 0) &= 0.3413 \\[5pt] P(X < 2) - 0.5 &= 0.3413 \\[5pt] P(X < 2) &= 0.8413 \\[5pt] P(X \leq 2) &= 0.8413 \end{align*}\]

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq 2) &= 0.8413 \\[5pt] P \left( Z \leq \dfrac{2-0}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.8413 \\[5pt] \Phi \left( \dfrac{2}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.8413 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{\sigma} &= \Phi^{-1} (0.8413 ) \end{align*} \]

According to the table, we have

\[ \Phi(1.00) = 0.8413 \quad \Rightarrow \quad \Phi^{-1}( 0.8413) = 1.00. \]

Therefore, we have

\[ \begin{align*} \dfrac{2}{\sigma} &= 1 \\[5pt] \sigma &= \dfrac{2}{1} \\[5pt] \sigma &= 2. \end{align*} \]

Finally,

\[\begin{align*} \sigma^2 &= (2)^2 = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4}. \end{align*}\]

question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X \sim N(3, \sigma^2)$ is a normal random variable with $P(1 < X < 5) = 0.3758,$ use the table to find $\sigma,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

$z$ $\, 0.07 \,$ $\, 0.08 \,$ $\, 0.09 \,$
$\, 0.4 \,$ $\, 0.6808 \,$ $\, 0.6844 \,$ $\, 0.6879 \,$
$\, 0.5 \,$ $\, 0.7157 \,$ $\, 0.7190 \,$ $\, 0.7224 \,$
$\, 0.6 \,$ $\, 0.7486 \,$ $\, 0.7517 \,$ $\, 0.7549 \,$

Hint: Note that the interval $1 < X < 5$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu=3.$
question.explanation:
First, note that the given interval is symmetric about the mean: \[ P(1 < X < 5) = P(3 - 2 < X < 3 + 2) \]

So, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry: \[\begin{align*} P(1 < X < 5) &= 0.3758 \\[5pt] 2 P(3 < X < 5) &= 0.3758 \\[5pt] P(3 < X < 5) &= 0.1879\\[5pt] P(X < 5) - P(X < 3) &= 0.1879 \\[5pt] P(X < 5) - 0.5 &= 0.1879 \\[5pt] P(X < 5) &= 0.6879 \\[5pt] P(X \leq 5) &= 0.6879 \end{align*}\]

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq 5) &= 0.6879 \\[5pt] P \left( Z \leq \dfrac{5-3}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.6879 \\[5pt] \Phi \left( \dfrac{2}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.6879 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{\sigma} &= \Phi^{-1} (0.6879 ) \\[5pt] \end{align*} \]

According to the table, we have

\[ \Phi(0.49) = 0.6879 \quad \Rightarrow \quad \Phi^{-1}( 0.6879) = 0.49. \]

Therefore, we have

\[ \begin{align*} \dfrac{2}{\sigma} &= 0.49 \\[5pt] \sigma &= \dfrac{2}{0.49} \\[5pt] \sigma& \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4.08} \end{align*} \]

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

example.title: Finding a Missing Parameter Using Symmetry When the Mean Is Nonzero

question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X \sim N(1, \sigma^2)$ is a normal random variable with $P(-2 < X < 4) = 0.6424,$ find $\sigma^2,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

$z$ $\, 0.01 \,$ $\, 0.02 \,$ $\, 0.03 \,$
$\, 0.9 \,$ $\, 0.8186 \,$ $\, 0.8212 \,$ $\, 0.8238 \,$
$\, 1.0 \,$ $\, 0.8438 \,$ $\, 0.8461 \,$ $\, 0.8485 \,$
$\, 1.1 \,$ $\, 0.8665 \,$ $\, 0.8686 \,$ $\, 0.8708 \,$

Hint: Note that the interval $-2 < X < 4$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu=1.$
question.explanation:
First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry: \[\begin{align*} P(-2 < X < 4) &= 0.6424 \\[5pt] 2 P(1 < X < 4) &= 0.6424 \\[5pt] P(1 < X < 4) &= 0.3212\\[5pt] P(X < 4) - P(X < 1) &= 0.3212 \\[5pt] P(X < 4) - 0.5 &= 0.3212 \\[5pt] P(X < 4) &= 0.8212 \\[5pt] P(X \leq 4) &= 0.8212 \end{align*}\]

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X \leq 4) &= 0.8212 \\[5pt] P \left( Z \leq \dfrac{4-1}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.8212 \\[5pt] \Phi \left( \dfrac{3}{\sigma} \right) &= 0.8212 \\[5pt] \dfrac{3}{\sigma} &= \Phi^{-1} (0.8212) \end{align*} \]

According to the table, we have

\[ \Phi(0.92) = 0.8212 \quad \Rightarrow \quad \Phi^{-1}( 0.8212 ) = 0.92. \]

Therefore, we have

\[\begin{align*} \dfrac{3}{\sigma} &= 0.92 \\[5pt] \sigma &= \dfrac{3}{0.92} \\[5pt] \sigma &\approx 3.260\,87. \end{align*}\]

Finally,

\[\begin{align*} \sigma^2 = (3.260\,87)^2 \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{10.63} \end{align*}\]

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
